channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Novel Telerehabilitation Interventions for Stress Urinary Incontinence : A Systematic Review of Randomised Controlled Trials.
item.description: A systematic review of 13 RCTs found telerehabilitation-delivered pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) to be a safe, feasible, and effective modality for stress urinary incontinence (SUI), showing significant subjective symptom reductions and improved quality of life, with comparable efficacy to conventional care.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Invisible Harms, Visible Benefits? Adverse Event Reporting in Physical Activity Interventions for Neurodevelopmental Disorders: A Meta-analysis and Critical Appraisal
item.description: This meta-analysis and critical appraisal examines adverse event reporting in physical activity interventions for individuals with neurodevelopmental disorders, finding that current reporting practices are inadequate.
item.author: Sports Med - Open

item.title: Tailoring Resistance Exercise for Knee Osteoarthritis: An Intervention Systematic Review With Dose-Response Meta-analysis of the Effects of Intensity and Volume.
item.description: A dose-response meta-analysis of 20 RCTs (n=791) found that isotonic resistance training may reduce pain (MD, -3.52 at 6000 repetitions), improve function (MD, -16.66 at 2600 repetitions), and increase muscle strength (standardized MD, 0.12 at 1600 repetitions) in knee OA patients, with moderate intensity yielding the greatest estimated benefits.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The Efficacy of Exercise Therapy for Nonspecific Chronic Low Back Pain According to the FITT Principle: A Systematic Review With Meta-analyses.
item.description: A systematic review with meta-analyses found that exercise therapy following the FITT principle is effective in reducing disability in individuals with nonspecific chronic low back pain.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Proximal and Distal Bimanual Motor Skill Learning After Stroke: Impairments, Trajectories, and Clinical Contributors
item.description: A randomized trial with 97 (sub)acute stroke patients found impairments in bimanual motor skill learning, particularly in distal upper limb segments, compared to healthy individuals.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Effects of ankle-foot orthosis-related conditions on muscle activity, spasticity, and psychosocial outcomes after stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 10 studies (N=931 participants) evaluated the effects of ankle-foot orthoses (AFOs) after stroke, finding uncertain effects on lower-limb muscle activity, spasticity, and psychosocial outcomes, despite their common use for gait improvement.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Proprioception Training and Surrogate Outcomes: A Systematic Review of Definitions, Measures, and Effectiveness Claims
item.description: A systematic review explored the definitions, measures, and effectiveness claims of proprioception training, revealing significant heterogeneity in its conceptualization and application across rehabilitation and sports practices.
item.author: Sports Medicine

item.title: Biological effects of technique-specific manual therapy in healthy individuals and people with musculoskeletal disorders: a systematic review with meta-analysis.
item.description: This systematic review with meta-analysis evaluates the neurophysiological and metabolic effects of technique-specific manual therapy (HVLA vs. non-HVLA) in healthy individuals and people with musculoskeletal disorders, registered prospectively in PROSPERO.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Liposuction versus conservative therapy for patients with lipoedema in Germany: a multicentre, randomised controlled clinical trial
item.description: A multicenter, randomized controlled clinical trial in Germany found liposuction to be superior to conservative therapy in reducing leg pain and improving quality of life for patients with lipoedema, despite being associated with a higher rate of serious adverse events.
item.author: The Lancet

item.title: Physiotherapist-led care for musculoskeletal conditions in the emergency department (RESHAP-ED): a randomised controlled trial with economic evaluation.
item.description: The RESHAP-ED randomized controlled trial found that physiotherapist-led care for musculoskeletal conditions in the emergency department significantly reduced length of stay and healthcare costs while maintaining non-inferior safety compared to usual care.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Paired comparison of extrinsic feedback effects on motor learning and functional recovery after stroke: a secondary analysis of randomized controlled trials.
item.description: A secondary analysis of randomized controlled trials (updated through November 2025) compared the effects of extrinsic feedback on motor learning versus functional recovery after stroke, calculating standardized mean differences using random-effects meta-analysis and accounting for within-study dependence.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Digital therapeutic combining exercise and cognitive-behavioural therapy reduces pain in patients with chronic patellofemoral pain: a multicentre randomised controlled trial.
item.description: An 8-week smartphone-based multidisciplinary digital therapeutic combining exercise and cognitive-behavioural therapy significantly reduced usual knee pain in 216 participants with chronic patellofemoral pain compared to education and exercise instruction.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Gait Speed Changes in Stroke Rehabilitation Motor Lower Extremity Randomized Controlled Trials by Intervention and Time Post-Stroke: A Meta-Analysis
item.description: A meta-analysis examined gait speed changes in randomized controlled trials of motor lower extremity stroke rehabilitation across various interventions, compared to conventional care or sham controls, at different time points post-stroke.
item.author: Archives of PM&R

item.title: Home-based digital exercise versus hospital physiotherapy for plantar fasciitis: a propensity-score-matched retrospective cohort study with dual-perspective cost-utility evaluation.
item.description: A propensity-score-matched retrospective cohort study in China (n=587) found that a 12-week home-based digital exercise program was non-inferior to hospital physiotherapy for 3-month first-step morning pain in plantar fasciitis (adjusted mean difference -0.63 points, 95% CI -0.92 to -0.35; p < 0.001) and was less costly from both payer and societal perspectives.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of an Integrated Treatment of Vestibular Rehabilitation and Cognitive Behavior Therapy for Chronic Dizziness in a Community-Based Population: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A single-blinded RCT (n=105) found that a group-based intervention integrating vestibular rehabilitation and cognitive behavioral strategies (VR-CBT) did not provide added benefit beyond a single-session brief vestibular intervention (BI-VR) in individuals with chronic dizziness for primary outcomes (dizziness-related handicap and preferred gait speed) at 6 and 12 months.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Living with stroke-related visual impairment: a qualitative exploration of lived experience, self-management, and support needs.
item.description: A qualitative study of 16 community-dwelling adults in Scotland explored lived experiences, self-management strategies, and unmet support needs in stroke-related visual impairment (SRVI). SRVI caused multidimensional impacts; self-developed strategies were common, but unmet needs included delayed assessment, limited tailored information, and misaligned rehabilitation.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Personalized FES-cycling patterns via optimal control: from musculoskeletal simulation to experimental validation
item.description: This study introduces an optimal control framework for functional electrical stimulation (FES) cycling that produces personalized stimulation patterns directly transferable from simulation to experimental cycling, aiming to improve rehabilitation for neurological patients.
item.author: J NeuroEng Rehabil

item.title: Addressing stroke family caregivers' mental health through person‑ and family‑centred rehabilitation.
item.description: This review summarizes literature on stroke family caregivers' experiences and support needs, proposing person- and family-centered care (PFCC) as a potential approach to address caregiver mental health challenges.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Determining the optimal volume of reactive balance training after stroke: a pilot randomized controlled trial
item.description: A three-arm pilot randomized controlled trial (n=36) explored the feasibility of delivering 1, 3, or 6 sessions of reactive balance training over 2-3 weeks for people with sub-acute stroke, aiming to inform the design of a larger optimal volume trial.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Muscle work during manual wheelchair propulsion in people with a spinal cord injury: a model-based approach.
item.description: This study used a modeling approach to evaluate the individual muscle contributions, particularly the rotator cuff muscles, to mechanical work during wheelchair propulsion in individuals with a spinal cord injury.
item.author: PubMed
